value.rationale: The exit-location distribution of a repelling focus is a natural transient transport observable absent from an exit-time survival law. The two single-exit phases, intervening three-channel phase, internal 3/4 transition, and independence of channel and number of visits yield testable, parameter-sensitive structure not obtained by a routine scalar area rescaling. The result has clear limitations to conditional area and the first exit, rather than overstating downstream impacts.
